e: The board of Thai Airways International decided to dismiss CEO Chai Eamsiri from his position with immediate effect.
Following three days of rainfall that resulted in flooding, authorities declare a disaster zone over Bangkok.
Thailand reduces visa-free stays for citizens of 60 countries from 60 days to 30 days.

Phra Wachirayan Wi, a former abbot at Wat Phutthaisawan in Ayutthaya, is arrested on suspicion of embezzling 100 million baht ($3 million) from the monastery and having inappropriate sexual relations.
A gunman fatally shoots a teacher at a kindergarten in Chonburi province.
An arson attack is carried out on a convenience store in Pattani province, resulting in two arrests.
At least two people are injured in a series of bombing and arson attacks across Narathiwat, Yala and Pattani provinces.
A French national is released on bail after an antisemitic attack that injured two Israeli women in Ko Pha-ngan.

Former MP Chalong Riewrang is arrested after fatally shooting Thongchai Yenprasert, the president of the Nonthaburi Provincial Administrative Organisation, and injuring his driver outside Thongchai's office.
At least nine people, including the 14-year-old assailant, are killed in a mass shooting in Nonthaburi.
A car crashes into a Kanchanaburi childcare center, injuring 16 people.
Killings of Diana and Roman Nazimova in Chonburi province.
The Wat Phra Mahathat temple in Nakhon Si Thammarat is designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The United States imposes a 12.5% tariff on Thailand, citing the presence of alleged forced labour in the supply chain.
Five paramilitary soldiers are killed and six others are injured after militants attack a security checkpoint in Narathiwat province.
Forty-one people are killed in a fire at a bar in Bangkok.
An 11-year-old child crashes a pickup truck into a group of monks on a pilgrimage walk in Mukdahan province, killing 11.
An Australian national is arrested after the body of 17-year old Tunchanok Donhomla is found in a suitcase in Pattaya.
The Bangkok South Criminal Court sentences two suspects to death over the 2015 Bangkok bombing.
Cambodia files a notice to UNCLOS seeking compulsory conciliation of its maritime border dispute with Thailand. On 5 June, Thailand agrees to send two representatives to the UNCLOS negotiations.
The inaugural all-star edition of Miss Grand International is held in Bangkok.
The Thai–Myanmar Friendship Bridge No.2 is opened for the first time in more than 10 months.
The government revises its visa policy and reduces visa-exemption periods for citizens of 93 countries.
A freight train crashes into a bus near Makkasan station in Bangkok, killing at least eight people and injuring 15 others.
Chadchart Sittipunt resigns as Governor of Bangkok ahead of the upcoming Bangkok gubernatorial election.
Former prime minister Thaksin Shinawatra is released from prison.
Thailand revokes a 2001 memorandum of understanding with Cambodia aimed at resolving maritime border disputes.
King Vajiralongkorn administers the oath of office to the cabinet members of Anutin Charnvirakul.
The Thailand national football team qualifies for the 2027 AFC Asian Cup after defeating Turkmenistan to finish top of their qualification group.
The House of Representatives reelects Anutin Charnvirakul as prime minister after the latter gains the support of 293 of 498 voting MPs.
A court in Bangkok sentences eSports players Naphat Warasin and Kong Sutprom to three months' imprisonment for cheating during the 2025 SEA Games.
Sophon Saram of the Bhumjaithai Party is elected Speaker of the House of Representatives.
The Government of Thailand summons Iran's ambassador, demanding an apology and an explanation for the attack on the bulk carrier MV Mayuree Naree in the waters of the Strait the previous day.

The Thailand-flagged bulk carrier MV Mayuree Naree is hit by two Iranian missiles shortly after passing the Strait of Hormuz. Twenty people are rescued and three are reported missing after the vessel catches on fire.

UNESCO announces the honorary recognition of Queen Rambai Barni as a World Important Person on the occasion of the 100th anniversary of her royal initiatives in education, social development, and gender equality. The celebration is based on the centenary of her investiture as Queen.
The Royal Thai Navy seizes a Cambodian fishing vessel along the maritime boundary between the two countries off the coast of Trat province.
At least 72 tigers are reported to have died following an outbreak of canine distemper at Tiger Kingdom in Chiang Mai.

The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission formally withdraws a defamation case it filed in a Thai court against Australian journalist and Thai resident Murray Hunter over articles published on his Substack newsletter after reaching a settlement.
Seven bomb attacks are made overnight on Yi-ngo and Ra-ngae districts in Narathiwat province.
The Bhumjaithai Party reaches an agreement to form a coalition government with the Pheu Thai Party.
